subject: Hotpatch shelving + network quarantine plan (FinServCorp private deployment)
messages:
From: FinServCorp Ops <ops@finservcorp.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com>, OnPrem Integrations <onprem-ops@vendor.example.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T09:21:00-07:00
Subject: Upcoming hotpatch window / network quarantine question

Hi Neha / OnPrem team,

We have an upcoming compliance-driven hotpatch target for our private deployment (FinServCorp VPC) and need to align on maintenance window, any network quarantine steps, and rollback guarantees. High level asks:  
- Can Redwood support a short quarantine that blocks east-west admin traffic for the patched cluster during the hotpatch?
- We need explicit rollback SLA (shelving to pinned version) if errors increase or latency regresses.
- What telemetry snapshot will you capture for an audit trail?

We’re aiming for a non-business hours window in the US (late Oct). Please propose a plan we can review with our SREs — include pinning strategy, canary size, and abort criteria.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
FinServCorp Ops
ops@finservcorp.com

Attachments: FinServ_maintenance_window_pref.pdf (see suggested windows)
From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com>
To: FinServCorp Ops <ops@finservcorp.com>
Cc: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.example.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming hotpatch window / network quarantine question

Samir — thanks, this is helpful. Draft plan below; want to make sure it fits your compliance checks before we lock the window. If this looks okay I’ll schedule a quick runbook dry-run with your SREs.

Planned window (proposal):
- Candidate: 2026-10-25 02:00 - 06:00 UTC (US-friendly overnight slot)
- Expected outage: none for API tier; potential 1–3 minute request spikes during canary swap.

Key actions (high level):
1) Version pinning: pin fleet to v1.12.3 post-patch (shelve previous v1.11.x if rollback needed).
2) Canary: start with 3 nodes (~5% traffic) for 30 minutes; run smoke tests and health probes.
3) Network quarantine: apply temporary ACL to block inter-cluster admin endpoints for nodes under patch; allow management plane from FinServCorp IPs only.
4) KV warming: pre-warm model KV caches and run a synthetic workload to validate response distribution.
5) Rollback/shelving criteria (immediate abort):
   - 3x baseline 5xx rate over 10 minutes OR
   - P95 latency > 300ms for 10 consecutive minutes OR
   - Canary failure of any structured-output regressions in eval set
6) Telemetry snapshot: retain 60-minute preflight and 120-minute postflight traces + token-level latency/throughput; we’ll export a tarball for your audit.

Owners and quick asks: 
- Irene: will own canary health checks and KV warm steps (see attached diffs).
- Vivek: confirm autoscaler gating and capacity buffer + isolation rules.
- Priyom: prepare rollback-playbook PDF and coordinate doc signature with FinServ change board.

Attachments: network-config-diff.patch.txt, rollback-playbook-v1.3.pdf

If that looks ok, I’ll schedule a 30-minute runbook dry-run the week of Oct 18.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.example.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.example.com>, FinServCorp Ops <ops@finservcorp.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hotpatch shelving + network quarantine plan (technical notes)

Looping in technical details — quick comments and additions: 

- Quarantine mechanism: prefer applying a short-lived iptables chain on the affected nodes managed via our orchestration (avoid cloud-provided ACL toggle when possible) so we can revert atomically. Patch will include the chain diff (attached network-config-diff.patch.txt).

- Canary sizing: 3 nodes is fine but ensure LB stickiness is drained before routing traffic. Steps: 1) cordon node; 2) drain; 3) apply patch & local smoke; 4) uncordon to join canary pool.

- Warm-up: KV cache warm-up must run with synthetic token sequences using same prefix distribution as your production prompts; failing to warm will produce tail-latency spikes. I’ll add the synthetic workload script to the runbook.

- Rollback execution: shelving will be performed by pinning the node’s runtime image to the last-known-good digest and issuing a coordinated fleet-wide rolling revert. Recovery checklist excerpt:
   * snapshot config -> store in S3 (immutable)
   * trigger rollout to pinned digest (shelve)
   * confirm KV state restored from preflight snapshot for canary nodes

- Audit evidence: we will bundle the pre/post telemetry and the orchestration event log (timestamps + operator id). Please confirm your retention window for evidence export (we currently have 30 days default).

Minor ask: FinServ, please confirm if you need KMS key rotation during the window — that would change our locking strategy and requires coordination.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-10-12T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hotpatch shelving + network quarantine plan (capacity and gating)

All — a few capacity/gating notes from infra: 

- Autoscaler: we need to lock the horizontal autoscaler scaling policies during the canary to prevent noise-induced scale-ups. I propose adding a temporary headroom buffer of 15% on the cluster and disabling PG-based scale triggers for the canary window.

- Preflight load test: run a 10-minute synthetic at 30% of peak qps targeting the canary nodes only; this verifies both latency and KV warm behavior.

- Metrics snapshot: create an immutable snapshot (we’ll copy to an external S3 bucket) that includes: token-level latency, cpu/gpu utilization, 5xx counts, and KV miss rates. We will attach the snapshot to JIRA INF-9837.

- Abort automation: if abort criteria hit, automation will: 1) stop traffic to patched nodes, 2) mark nodes drained, 3) trigger shelving playbook (attached rollback-playbook-v1.3.pdf). Manual confirmation still required from Red team lead to avoid irrelevant rollbacks.

Irene — I agree with iptables approach. Priyom — can you update the playbook to include the autoscaler lock steps?

—Vivek
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Hotpatch shelving + network quarantine plan (ack / follow-ups)

Neha / team — thanks, that plan reads well. A couple of follow-ups before we confirm the dry-run: 
1) Retention: we need the audit bundle retained for 90 days; please confirm you can export the telemetry snapshot to our secure S3 and set TTL accordingly.
2) KMS rotation: we will not rotate KMS during the window; we’ll plan a separate maintenance for that.
3) Air-gapped nodes: we have a small subset of on-prem nodes that will be fully air-gapped during the patch; please document any manual steps required for those hosts in the runbook.

Once you update the runbook with autoscaler-lock and air-gap notes we’ll confirm the dry-run for Oct 19.

Samir Patel
FinServCorp Ops
